Richard Bornemann∗†
Inria - Flowers Team
richard.bornemann@inria.fr

Abstract
Recent works have proven that intricate cooperative behaviors can emerge in
agents trained using meta reinforcement learning on open ended task distribu-
tions using self-play. While the results are impressive, we argue that self-play and
other centralized training techniques do not accurately reflect how general col-
lective exploration strategies emerge in the natural world: through decentralized
training and over an open-ended distribution of tasks. In this work we there-
fore investigate the emergence of collective exploration strategies, where several
agents meta-learn independent recurrent policies on an open ended distribution of
tasks. To this end we introduce a novel environment with an open ended proce-
durally generated task space which dynamically combines multiple subtasks sam-
pled from five diverse task types to form a vast distribution of task trees. We show
that decentralized agents trained in our environment exhibit strong generalization
abilities when confronted with novel objects at test time. Additionally, despite
never being forced to cooperate during training the agents learn collective explo-
ration strategies which allow them to solve novel tasks never encountered during
training. We further find that the agents learned collective exploration strategies
extend to an open ended task setting, allowing them to solve task trees of twice the
depth compared to the ones seen during training. Our open source code as well as
videos of the agents can be found on our companion website

See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**.
